acquisition.isolation: Each product-fixture run receives a fresh fixture copy and private HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, npm prefix, and product cache. No index or process is shared across products.
acquisition.network_policy: Only version-pinned package or release acquisition may use the network. All measured prepare, query, update, and cleanup steps run offline.
acquisition.source_clone_policy: If a source checkout is unavoidable, clone its pinned tag with --depth 1 --filter=blob:none. Never clone mutable default branches.

adapter_contract.actual_command_rule: Every substituted argv and MCP method/arguments envelope is stored in the execution record.
adapter_contract.file_level_test_rule: Adapters encode a selected whole test file as path::*. The evaluator expands it only against the independently committed test_inventory. Unknown or ambiguous file selections remain false positives.
adapter_contract.freshness_rule: After a mutation, use the product's documented watched/incremental behavior. A product with no update mode is queried normally so its own cache invalidation behavior is measured. Never force a cold rebuild unless the native workflow requires it and the record says so.
adapter_contract.native_tool_rule: Use the documented native query closest to the requested relation. Do not supplement a result with grep, another competitor, or evaluator data.
adapter_contract.normalization_rule: Normalize only separators, repository prefixes, documented symbol wrappers, and native node IDs that map unambiguously to path::symbol. Ambiguous matches stay in the answer and become false positives.
adapter_contract.pagination_rule: Consume all native pages up to the frozen output and timeout limits; count every request as one tool call and every delivered UTF-8 response byte.
adapter_contract.source_freshness_rule: Definition retrieval must also return native source evidence containing the state-specific frozen marker. If the product exposes no source in an applicable native definition/context operation, definition freshness for body_edit is UNSUPPORTED rather than guessed from the filesystem.
adapter_contract.test_identity_rule: The oracle declares test nodes by committed test-file path and symbol, including exported TypeScript/TSX test declarations. Native filename/framework heuristics are measured; adapters do not redefine the oracle.
adapter_contract.unsupported_rule: Return UNSUPPORTED only when the pinned product exposes no applicable native operation. Do not infer an empty answer.

campaign_order: Commit policy, corpus, oracle, adapter API, scorer, resource guard, unit tests, documentation, and release-note entry.
Complete Girder normal and watch adapters end-to-end.
Complete ripwire as the first external adapter and run the full tiny-python campaign.

Integrate and run each remaining product one at a time after its concrete adapter is frozen, choosing the lowest-resource reproducible official distribution next; perform process cleanup and memory preflight between products.
Generate immutable JSON, CSV, Markdown report, environment metadata, setup-friction records, and raw artifacts.

competitors.identity_normalization: Map crate module segments to the unique fixture source path. For Rust, also map conventional crate module foo to src/foo.rs or src/foo/mod.rs; keep root-level paths without a native file identity unresolved.

native_queries.definition: find_definition followed by get_source for the one exact node (2 calls)

projection.callees: All semantic paths in the ask_codebase callees response except the seed; direct only by native query contract.
projection.callers: All semantic paths in the ask_codebase callers response except the seed; direct only by native query contract.
projection.definition: exact find_definition node; get_source text is source evidence
projection.impact: All semantic paths in the ask_codebase impact response except the seed.

competitors.install_cwd: A private copy containing the committed GitNexus package.json and package-lock.json.

native_queries.impact: impact direction=upstream maxDepth=32 includeTests=true with full pagination
native_queries.tests: impact direction=upstream maxDepth=32 includeTests=true, filtered to frozen test paths

projection.callees: context outgoing entries whose relation is CALLS
projection.callers: context incoming entries whose relation is CALLS
projection.impact: impact byDepth symbol identities only, all pages, excluding seed
projection.tests: impact byDepth identities whose normalized path is a frozen corpus test path

competitors.runtime_placement: Install the exact committed npm lock into a fresh local temporary directory because the ChromeOS removable 9p mount rejects required npm .bin symlinks. Keep the reusable npm acquisition cache external; each campaign still receives a fresh local HOME and product data directory.

competitors.freshness: Keep the indexed MCP session open and apply filesystem mutations normally. Do not force reindexing. The product-owned watcher and the frozen evaluator probe loop determine current, stale, rebuilding, or unchanged answers.

native_queries.callees: trace_path direction=outbound depth=1 mode=calls include_tests=true format=json limit=500 with cursor pagination
native_queries.callers: trace_path direction=inbound depth=1 mode=calls include_tests=true format=json limit=500 with cursor pagination
native_queries.definition: search_graph name_pattern=^{target}$ format=json limit=500 with offset pagination, then get_code_snippet (2 calls for one exact declaration)
native_queries.impact: trace_path direction=inbound depth=32 mode=calls include_tests=true format=json limit=500 with cursor pagination
native_queries.tests: the same inbound depth=32 trace_path result, restricted to native identities in test-shaped paths

projection.callees: trace_path outbound rows at depth exactly 1, mapped from native qualified-name prefixes to one fixture file.
projection.callers: trace_path inbound rows at depth exactly 1, mapped from native qualified-name prefixes to one fixture file.
projection.definition: Exact-name search_graph groups map their native file and qualified name to path::symbol; get_code_snippet source is freshness evidence.
projection.impact: all inbound trace_path rows through depth 32, excluding the seed because the native response omits it.
projection.tests: impact projection restricted by language-native test path shape; the adapter does not read oracle.json.

competitors.runtime_placement: Verify the official archive checksum, extract it externally, then copy that exact binary once to a mode-0700 local temporary runtime directory. Use a fresh mode-0700 local HOME and CBM_CACHE_DIR per campaign. Direct execution/cache on the ChromeOS removable mount failed the pinned product security and 30-second executable-identity admission checks; both raw failures are retained.

competitors.freshness: After each filesystem mutation, synchronously await build_or_update_graph_tool with full_rebuild=false and postprocess=minimal, then begin the common query probe loop.

native_queries.definition: semantic_search_nodes_tool query={target} kind=Function limit=500 detail_level=standard, then get_review_context_tool for the unique returned file with include_source=true max_depth=0 max_files=1
native_queries.impact: semantic_search_nodes_tool exact-name target lookup, then get_impact_radius_tool changed_files=[returned_file] max_depth=64 detail_level=standard (native implementation limit 500)

projection.callees: query_graph_tool callees_of result identities; unresolved native identities remain false positives.
projection.callers: query_graph_tool callers_of result identities; unresolved native identities remain false positives.
projection.definition: Exact-name Function search results map native file_path and name to path::symbol; get_review_context_tool source_snippets for the unique file supply source freshness evidence.
projection.impact: get_impact_radius_tool impacted_nodes with kind other than File, excluding the seed because it is returned in changed_nodes.

competitors.runtime_placement: Use a fresh mode-0700 local HOME and CRG_DATA_DIR for each campaign while fixtures and raw artifacts remain external. SQLite graph creation on the ChromeOS removable 9p mount failed with disk I/O error; the retained local-data retry passed.

native_queries.tests: --affected={target} XML; selected test files normalize as path::*

projection.definition: Exact-name sig rows become path::name; the matching expanded body is source evidence.
projection.tests: Every native <test p=...> file becomes p::* and expands to all frozen test nodes in that file during scoring.

competitors.query_pagination: --limit=500 and --offset=N only on callers, callees, and impact; --for and --affected are fixed reports and reject pagination flags

freeze_rule: This policy, corpus.json, oracle.json, scorer, adapter contract, and their unit tests must be committed before any comparative campaign. Campaign results may not change them.

host_limits.description: Low-resource ChromeOS Crostini measurement host; results are host-specific.
host_limits.on_unsafe_memory: Do not launch, or terminate the process tree if already running, cleanup, and record RESOURCE_BLOCKED. Never weaken the host or threshold after seeing results.
host_limits.proc_race_handling: A process disappearing during /proc enumeration is normal. OSError while reading a sampled process is ignored; the next 100 ms sample observes the remaining process group.
host_limits.process_supervision: Every external process is placed in its own process group. The runner samples the full descendant tree RSS at 100 ms, parses /proc stat after the final parenthesized process-name delimiter so spaces or right parentheses cannot shift fields, terminates above the frozen RSS cap or below emergency system headroom, enforces bounded output and timeout, and kills descendants during cleanup. This supervisor must pass unit tests before acquisition or campaign execution.

limitations: This benchmark measures small frozen fixtures on one low-resource Chromebook container; it does not establish universal performance or large-repository behavior.
It measures these pinned versions and native interfaces, not every product capability or configuration.

Girder natural-language search remains experimental, impacted_tests remains advisory, dynamic dispatch can be missed, and watched updates reuse parsing while still performing project-wide semantic resolution.
Bytes are bytes. No tokenizer is run.
A static frozen oracle cannot establish correctness on code patterns absent from the corpus.

measurements.calls: Every native CLI invocation or MCP tools/call request. Model requests are not used.
measurements.cold_setup_index_seconds: Acquisition/install excluded; starts immediately before product preparation and ends at first ready response.
measurements.freshness_probe: After each mutation, query all five kinds in the fixed order, skipping only native UNSUPPORTED kinds. Current source-marker evidence is required for definition. First correct usable answer occurs when every supported query in one probe set is PASS. Poll every 250 ms. Three identical completed WRONG or ERROR probe sets may terminate only after 2 seconds and only when no applicable result is STALE. Any STALE result resets the terminal stability window. TIMEOUT and RESOURCE_BLOCKED terminate immediately. If every kind is unsupported, the mutation is UNSUPPORTED. At the 120-second readiness deadline, preserve STALE, ERROR, or WRONG from the last probe instead of relabeling it as a request timeout. Non-PASS mutations have null update-to-correct latency; their first/last probe elapsed, calls, bytes, and statuses remain recorded.
measurements.peak_memory: Maximum observed process-tree RSS when available; null otherwise. It is never inferred.
measurements.preflight_boundary: Adapter response-shape probes are INVALIDATED_PREFLIGHT or PREFLIGHT_PASS, retained with raw output, and excluded from all scores and timings. Each product campaign begins only after the current policy and its concrete adapter checkpoint are committed.
measurements.raw_artifacts: Write complete stdout and stderr for every invocation. If combined output exceeds 4 MiB, terminate and record ERROR with the retained capped streams and byte limit.
measurements.repetitions: Exactly one cold prepare, one unmeasured warm-up per supported query at base state, and one measured warm query. Mutation measurements are one cumulative sequence per product-fixture; no retries except frozen readiness polling.
measurements.response_bytes: Exact UTF-8 bytes delivered on native stdout/stderr or MCP response envelopes, before normalization. Initial prompts and harness prose do not exist and are excluded.
measurements.test_granularity: Function-level predictions score directly. Whole-file predictions expand to every committed test in that file, reflecting actual execution and charging unrelated tests as false positives.
measurements.tokens: Not measured and no token-saving claim is permitted.
measurements.update_latency_seconds: Filesystem mutation completion to first correct usable answer. Poll requests and bytes are counted and retained.
measurements.warm_query_correctness: Warm-up and measured query are independently scored. A measured cost is retained beside its status; cross-product cost comparison requires the same supported task and reports correctness alongside cost.
measurements.warm_query_seconds: Wall time around the native query after a successful warm-up of the identical query; the warm-up is separately recorded.

oracle.access: Evaluator only. Adapter modules and competitor process trees must not receive this path or its contents.
oracle.calls: Direct runtime call relationships. The frozen function-parameter edge is included even when static products miss it.
oracle.impact: Reverse-transitive runtime callers, excluding the target.
oracle.matching_wrong_answers: Two products returning the same wrong answer are each WRONG.
oracle.test_inventory: Each state lists every test node in the fixture. A native whole-test-file prediction expands to every listed node in that file before scoring; this models what will run and retains unrelated nodes as false positives.
oracle.tests: Test nodes in the reverse-transitive impact set.

primary_question: Does Girder have a defensible measured advantage in trustworthy coding-agent context and blast-radius/change analysis on this frozen corpus?
required_report_sections: What This Benchmark Does NOT Establish

scope.aggregate_population: tiny-python is an adapter/scorer gate and is excluded from comparative aggregates. The four modest language fixtures are the aggregate population.
scope.larger_repository: Optional only after the frozen tiny and modest campaign completes. Its corpus and oracle require a separately committed additive policy before execution.
scope.product_changes: Forbidden during this campaign. Product defects remain measured defects.

scoring.aggregate_rule: Macro-average per task and report counts. Do not silently omit losses or failures.
scoring.comparison_rule: Operational costs may be compared on common supported tasks and must retain their correctness status. Never call unsupported, timeout, install failure, or resource failure a Girder win.
scoring.definition: PASS only for exact set equality; also report precision, recall, and F1.
scoring.failure_numeric_treatment: Precision/recall/F1 macro values include only queries that returned a parseable answer (PASS, WRONG, or STALE). Every table also reports eligible-task denominator, parsed-answer denominator, and all status counts. UNSUPPORTED, TIMEOUT, RESOURCE_BLOCKED, INSTALL_FAILED, and ERROR are never converted to zero or omitted from status counts.
scoring.freshness: PASS for the current oracle; STALE when the answer exactly equals the distinct preceding oracle or the product explicitly reports stale/rebuilding; WRONG for any other completed wrong answer.
scoring.relations: Set precision=TP/(TP+FP), recall=TP/(TP+FN), and harmonic F1. Empty/empty has precision=recall=1. Empty against nonempty has both 0 where applicable.
scoring.test_priority: Report precision and recall separately; never collapse a missed required test into an accuracy-only score.
scoring.whole_file_staleness: Expand a file prediction against the current inventory for current scoring and separately against the prior inventory for prior-oracle staleness. Never pass the current expanded answer as the prior expected answer.
